newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemalan farmers grateful for mine clearing.
newsitem.headline: Guatemalan farmers grateful for mine clearing.

text.p: A project to clear mines left over from Guatemala's civil war will help to calm the fears some coffee farmers had of returning to their fields, farmers said on Friday.

"The truth is we are poor people who don't have another way to earn a living. Now that they are de-mining some of my family and friends are free to go again to clean up their coffee farms," Honourio Vasquez, a farmer who lives near the Tajamulco Volcano, told reporters.

United Nations experts and former rebels of the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) began removing mines on March 17 and have deactivated 182 of an estimated 350 explosives buried on Tajamulco, Guatemala's highest volcano, 25 miles (40 kms) from the Mexico border.
The URNG placed mines on Tajamulco in the early and mid-1980s in one of the most violent periods of Guatemala's 36-year civil war, to protect a strategic radio transmitter.

Vasquez said villagers who ignored warning signs placed on the volcano by the guerrillas risked death or dismemberment. After a mine injured one person, farming on the mountain dropped off completely.
Rebel leaders provided a map of the mines under terms of a historic peace agreement in December that ended Central America's last armed conflict.
